entries.label: MHRC staff investigative report, 26 Jun 2026
entries.anchor: there is a probable cause to believe that OHS’s administration of federally-funded housing programs did not comply with Title VI requirements
entries.claim: The full staff investigative report underlying the probable-cause determination (MHRC-ED-DETERMINATION adopts this report's Findings of Fact by reference). Covers an OHS program that placed 8 families from Nashville Rescue Mission overflow into units at The Ave and Hillside Crossing (Aug 2024-Sep 2025): no complete written policy for participant selection ever produced ("OHS has not responded to requests"), conflicting accounts on whether Coordinated Entry was used, rent assistance cut/restructured under a described "breakdown plan" leading to eviction/lease-violation notices, 2 of 8 families never got the promised housing vouchers, and a former Step Up employee who resigned after declining to revise a written statement (Findings 21-23). 6 of the 8 women participants (75%) identify as Black. As written, this document contains no complainant names -- refers throughout to "the complainant" and unnamed witnesses -- so no redaction was needed on this copy. IMPORTANT: probable cause is an investigative threshold, explicitly NOT a finding of liability (the ED's own determination letter says so directly) -- report it as what MHRC found sufficient evidence to investigate further, not as an adjudicated fact.

entries.label: MHRC Executive Director probable cause determination, 30 Jun 2026 (redacted)
entries.anchor: there is probable cause to believe that the administration of federally funded housing assistance
entries.claim: Executive Director Davie Tucker Jr.'s determination letter, adopting MHRC-STAFF-INVESTIGATIVE-REPORT's Findings of Fact by reference. This is the document The Contributor (CTB-TACKETT-AUG26) quotes verbatim without ever linking -- the anchor text matches that reporting exactly, confirming this is the actual source. Lays out a ~10-month procedural history (Aug 28 2025 HubNashville inquiry through Jun 26 2026 staff report): OHS's PIO told MHRC in Oct 2025 the matter was 'not a Title VI issue' and that the individuals were 'no longer eligible... because they were "no longer homeless"'; OHS did not respond to multiple meeting requests; a formal complaint was filed Jan 23, 2026 after informal efforts failed. Determination: probable cause found; complaint upheld; advances to formal conciliation. Complainant names are redacted (blacked out) in the copy supplied to this project -- preserved as-is, not a redaction this project performed or could reverse. Explicitly states: 'probable cause is not a finding of guilt... Nothing in this Determination constitutes a final finding of discrimination or liability.'

entries.claim: IMPORTANT: this is Councilmember Ginny Welsch's own letter to the Metro Audit Committee -- an allegation and audit-request document, NOT an audit finding, despite the filename 'OHS Audit Executive Summary.pdf'. It is signed by Welsch, not the Office of Internal Audit, and itemizes the $3.2M+ figure into named components (DePaul/L-6054 invoices $568,923; Landlord Engagement funds $565,577; a single department credit card $130,109 plus $46,994.14 in reimbursements, including a $1,800 charge to 'WP COLEYSJJ' Welsch states 'appears to be' Coley's Jook Junt 'operated by Director Calvin's sister'; ARPA funding-cliff exposure $2,000,000; 'temporary service' miscoding $11,000,000; and others), plus safety-incident and staffing allegations at Strobel House. Every figure and claim in this document is Welsch's own characterization, sourced in her footnotes mostly to PRR-obtained documents on Google Drive/Sites that this project has not yet accessed or verified independently. Do not cite any figure from this document as an established fact -- attribute it to Welsch's letter specifically. The Coley's Jook Junt / 'Director Calvin's sister' claim is now attributable to a named, on-record source (Welsch, in a letter to the Audit Committee) rather than an untraceable rumor, which is a real change from this project's earlier note on COLEYS-JOOK-JUNT/NASHVILLEVOYAGER-SHATICKA -- but Welsch's own footnote 6 for that line cites only a 'Reimbursement expense' record, not a family-relationship document, so the relationship itself is still not independently verified by any source this project has seen.

entries.label: Shanley Deignan email on CoC ranking decision, 6 Aug 2026 (forwarded 19 Sep 2026)
entries.anchor: decision that was made not to fund HMIS
entries.claim: Shanley Deignan, chair of the Continuum of Care Charter Committee and HMIS Oversight committee (Park Center Nashville), writes to HPC members objecting to the decision not to submit HMIS and Coordinated Entry renewal projects in the 2026 CoC competition. Key substance: (1) the decision was placed before the HPC at the last minute without community input; (2) this year the General Membership was due to elect/re-elect the HMIS and CE Lead roles per the charter, and removing the dollars bypasses that charter process -- notes the 2023 working group deferred the HMIS/CE lead selection 2-3 years after making OHS the Collaborative Applicant, which brings the question due now; OHS is named as the current designated lead agency holding these dollars; (3) warns from TA experience with another Middle Tennessee CoC that losing HMIS/CE dollars collapsed the CoC into emergency HUD support and volunteer operation for over a year; (4) Metro backfill is acknowledged but flagged as fragile across budget cycles, leadership change, and fiscal priorities; (5) asks HPC to keep the topic on the monthly agenda, hold a transparent General Membership conversation on lead-selection authority, and create contracts between each Lead role and the community. Includes a second embedded message (29 Jul 2026 to the Executive Committee/PEC) with five documented questions: one-year vs permanent strategy, written Metro commitment and duration, lead-election mechanics without money, accountability without CoC dollars, and Metro-budget-change risk. CAVEATS: forwarded Gmail export (Deignan to Mike Lacy, 19 Sep 2026, forwarding Deignan's 6 Aug 2026 HPC message); authenticity rests on provenance, not on an independently fetched URL. References an attached 'Collaborative Applicant Application' / 'CAA Final Draft.docx (31K)' that is named in the PDF but not included with it. The Park Center confidentiality/HIPAA footer is boilerplate on the forwarded mail, not a classification of the CoC content. CORRECTION 2026-09-19 (private, via journalist relay -- not a captured document, no bytes held): Deignan corrected the term timeline as stated in the email -- HMIS is in year 3 of a 5-year term, and CE is in year 8 of a 5-year term ("Literally 8"), i.e. CE is about 3 years overdue and, per Deignan, no one had ever raised it. Asked whether that meant a re-election should have happened, the relayed answer was yes; CE and HMIS oversight are going to host shared meetings soon to develop that process. Treat as an on-background source correction pending on-record confirmation; do not publish the relayed wording as a verbatim quote without Deignan's permission. (Relay reads "shard meetings"; taken as "shared meetings", sic preserved.)
